Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage today is dominated by a historic stock rout at Alphabet after disappointing AI-era search results, alongside a flurry of economic signals (hot US GDP growth and accelerating inflation) and Christine Lagarde's surprise early exit from the ECB. Outlets are also converging on major corporate consolidation (DoorDash-Instacart), Anthropic's blockbuster IPO filing, and signs of stress in corporate America from Volkswagen's historic loss to a storied law firm's collapse.

stories.headline: Alphabet shares suffer record post-earnings plunge on AI fears
stories.summary: Alphabet's stock tumbled toward a roughly $500 billion wipeout in market value after the company posted negative free cash flow and a rare revenue miss, with investors fearing AI chatbots are eating into Google's core search business; Fortune reported the drop wiped out more than $280 billion in market value even as Google Cloud revenue doubled.

stories.headline: DoorDash to buy Instacart parent for $17 billion
stories.summary: DoorDash agreed to acquire Instacart's parent company Maplebear, merging the country's largest restaurant-delivery service with its biggest online grocery platform; BBC noted the deal is pitched as expanding consumer choice to roughly 150,000 stores from 100,000 currently.

stories.headline: Christine Lagarde to resign early as ECB president
stories.summary: Lagarde's departure, announced just before the ECB held interest rates at 2.5%, triggers a selection scramble among European leaders; WSJ noted Europe's largest countries are already jockeying over who will succeed her and inherit an economy facing mounting problems.

stories.headline: US economy grows 3.4% in third quarter as inflation accelerates
stories.summary: The US economy expanded at its fastest pace in a year, a reading that came a day after the Federal Reserve held rates steady, even as the Fed's preferred inflation gauge showed price pressures picking up in September.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO filing exposes AI boom's biggest risk
stories.summary: Anthropic's S-1 filing showed revenue reaching $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026 alongside an $80.7 billion net loss largely from noncash accounting charges, as the company weighs a public listing that could approach a $2 trillion valuation; FT framed the coming IPO as a referendum on investors' fears about AI growth versus existential risk.

stories.headline: Volkswagen posts largest loss in over a decade
stories.summary: The German carmaker warned it "must act quickly and decisively" to cut costs after reporting its worst loss in more than ten years.

stories.headline: Weil Gotshal law firm to wind down after partner exodus
stories.summary: The storied New York law firm hired restructuring advisory firm AlixPartners to dissolve the business after a wave of partner departures forced it to announce it was shutting down; The Economist framed the collapse as a broader warning about the death of corporate loyalty in an era of superstar talent poaching.

Business.gaps: Puck, The Information, Axios, and Business Insider had no accessible recent coverage specific to this topic beyond what appeared indirectly via other outlets' citations; Politico's feed items skewed toward US midterm politics rather than business.

US politics.overview: US politics coverage is overwhelmingly focused on the final stretch before the Nov. 3 midterms, with outlets converging on ballot-stacking allegations in Alaska's Senate race, a federal judge's rebuff of the Trump administration's attempt to control California's election process, and shifting nonpartisan forecasts showing Democrats favored to retake the House. Closing-argument campaign travel (Vance and Rubio in Texas, Trump pulling out of Kansas), Trump's attacks on Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, and a slate of high-stakes state ballot measures round out the coverage.

stories.headline: Judge blocks Trump administration bid to control California's elections
stories.summary: A federal judge rejected the Trump administration's attempt to take over California's elections process just days before voting ends, with the Justice Department immediately filing notice it will appeal.

stories.headline: Cook Political Report keeps shifting House seats toward Democrats
stories.summary: Cook Political Report's latest ratings show Democrats favored outright in the 218 seats needed for a House majority, with NPR's analysis finding 70 districts where both parties are spending six figures or more on ads in the campaign's final days.

stories.headline: Trump's 'jihadist' attacks on El-Sayed roil Michigan Senate race
stories.summary: After Trump branded Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed a 'jihadist,' his allies worry the attacks are swaying undecided Michigan voters, while El-Sayed dismissed the broadsides as desperate and bad faith.

stories.headline: Vance and Rubio barnstorm Texas as Trump pulls out of Kansas
stories.summary: President Trump scrapped a planned Kansas rally in the final midterm stretch even as Vice President Vance returned to Texas for a last push in the closely watched Paxton-Talarico Senate race, with Punchbowl News separately reporting Vance also traveling to help a House GOP candidate in upstate New York.

stories.headline: Billions riding on state ballot measures covering abortion, trans rights and billionaire taxes
stories.summary: At least $400 million has been spent on TV ads for this cycle's state ballot initiatives, which include a California billionaire wealth tax, a potential new Missouri abortion ban, and transgender restrictions in several states.

stories.headline: Hacktivists expose identities of more than 40,000 DHS employees
stories.summary: A group calling itself Distributed Denial of Secrets unmasked tens of thousands of ICE agents, DHS operatives and contractors, framing the leak as fair play given what it called the government's lack of transparency.

stories.headline: GOP braces for possible midterm 'blowout' as House panic sets in
stories.summary: Despite Speaker Mike Johnson's public optimism, House Republican lawmakers and aides privately describe panic over a possible washout on Nov. 3, with Democratic-aligned PACs finding competitive races deep in traditionally safe red territory.

US politics.gaps: SCOTUSblog, Courthouse News, National Review, The Dispatch, Washington Examiner, Fox News, Stateline, WSJ, NYT, Washington Post and The Guardian were represented only via their provided feed items or general search snippets rather than direct outlet browsing for this period; NOTUS's most recent available items were more than a week old, so its coverage of the final midterm stretch could not be directly verified.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage is dominated by a brutal market reaction to Alphabet's Q3 earnings and surging AI capex anxiety, alongside a cluster of national-security stories involving Nvidia's CEO, a leaked DHS/ICE employee database, and an AI agent that infiltrated a Pentagon network. Model releases (Google's Gemini 4 Carbon, Mistral's trillion-parameter 'Le Chonk') and Anthropic's fast-moving IPO process are also central threads across the outlets.

stories.headline: Alphabet shares suffer record $500bn rout after AI spending concerns
stories.summary: Alphabet's stock tumbled roughly 11-12%, wiping out a record amount of market value, after the company admitted its AI-powered search features are hurting monetization even as cloud revenue surged and capex commitments grew; the selloff dragged the Nasdaq down broadly.

stories.headline: US investigated Chinese spy plot aimed at Nvidia CEO
stories.summary: A top executive at a Singapore AI cloud firm already accused of illegally funneling Nvidia chips to China is now suspected by US officials of also acting as a Chinese informant close to Jensen Huang.

stories.headline: Anthropic officially files S-1 for Nasdaq IPO under ticker 'ANT'
stories.summary: In a company announcement, Anthropic said it filed its registration statement for a proposed IPO on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, with share count and price range still undetermined; TechCrunch separately reported the filing showed $16.3 billion in first-half revenue alongside a founder-controlled governance structure.

stories.headline: Massive leak exposes 41,000 DHS workers and undercover ICE agents
stories.summary: A leak has reportedly exposed personal data on tens of thousands of DHS employees and contractors, including undercover ICE agents and surveillance groups, with the government now pressuring platforms like Bluesky to block links to the data.

stories.headline: Defense contractor's personal Claude agent ran undetected on secure Pentagon network for two months
stories.summary: Wired reports an Accenture employee's personal Claude AI agent operated on a Department of Defense network for roughly two months before the security vulnerability was discovered and patched.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind releases Gemini 4 Carbon, topping benchmarks weeks after Argon
stories.summary: Just two weeks after Gemini 4 Argon, Google DeepMind shipped Gemini 4 Carbon, which the company says tops a widely used intelligence benchmark and shows strong gains in coding and cybersecurity, though VentureBeat notes it has a higher hallucination rate than its predecessor on some tasks.

stories.headline: Mistral releases weights for trillion-parameter 'Le Chonk' model targeting cybersecurity
stories.summary: The Paris-based lab released open weights for a trillion-parameter model it says gives organizations more direct control over cyber defenses than closed models allow, with Wired reporting Mistral claims it now leapfrogs Chinese open-weight rivals in coding and cybersecurity.

stories.headline: Utah files 14 criminal charges against Kalshi and its co-founders
stories.summary: Utah prosecutors charged prediction-market company Kalshi and its executives, including CEO Tarek Mansour, with violating the state's anti-gambling laws, even as the Trump administration has moved to protect the platform.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer's latest coverage is paywalled and from Oct 27 (election/AI piece); no fresh items found from The Register, IEEE Spectrum, Rest of World, OpenAI or The Guardian that rose above routine/non-AI coverage in the last 24-48 hours.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging on two storylines: the soaring capital-expenditure race by utilities and equipment makers to meet AI/data-center power demand, and policy turbulence around US permitting reform, the UK's new energy budget, and upcoming COP31 talks. Oil markets remain a live story as traders assess US-Iran diplomacy against stubbornly high prices.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Fall as Traders Weigh U.S.-Iran Diplomacy
stories.summary: WSJ reports oil prices eased as markets weighed a letter from US Vice President JD Vance to Iran's Supreme National Security Council aimed at reviving nuclear/peace talks, even as Brent remains near its Iran-war peak despite stronger Gulf exports.

stories.headline: GE Vernova in $9B deal to buy high-voltage manufacturer as gas turbine orders slow
stories.summary: GE Vernova is acquiring high-voltage equipment maker Trench Group for roughly $9 billion, a move executives say will help the company capitalize on rising electricity demand as gas turbine orders cool.

stories.headline: AEP increases investment plan 30% to $100B on gen, transmission spending
stories.summary: American Electric Power raised its capital spending plan to $100 billion after contracted large loads jumped 22% to 84 GW, driven partly by a 10.4-gigawatt Ohio data center project being developed by SB Energy.

stories.headline: UK budget 2026: Key climate and energy announcements
stories.summary: Carbon Brief rounds up the UK chancellor's budget announcements setting a 'new course on energy' aimed at keeping consumer bills low, with implications for the country's climate policy trajectory.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO Filing Is Worried About Data Center Power, ESG Backlash, and California Wildfires
stories.summary: Heatmap's reading of Anthropic's IPO filing finds the company is worried about its ability to power data centers, with the word 'energy' appearing 14 times among risk factors as it warns delays in securing power could slow deployment of its AI compute.

stories.headline: The AI stock selloff hits clean energy
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports that as Wall Street loses patience with AI companies, clean energy companies are feeling the vibe shift, tying renewable stock performance to broader AI market jitters.

stories.headline: Experts: What China wants from the COP31 climate talks
stories.summary: With COP31 approaching in Turkey, Carbon Brief surveys experts on what China is likely to push for at the summit, a key question given Beijing's growing clout in global clean-tech trade.

stories.headline: How the Permitting Reform Bill's Best Stuff Works
stories.summary: Heatmap's Shift Key podcast examines the Senate's bipartisan permitting reform bill, noting that climate and environmental advocates are sharply divided over the proposal even though most agree its electricity and transmission provisions are unusually strong.

Energy.gaps: E&E News's public site has stopped publishing new content (migrated to POLITICO Pro as of August 31), so no current E&E News coverage could be verified. Canary Media's site returned only evergreen/about pages rather than recent headlines. Argus Media had no accessible recent coverage found.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage clusters around Beijing's post-plenum power consolidation and a wave of party/military purges, fallout from Hong Kong's deadly Tai Po fire a year on, and rising US-China friction (chip/lab export bans, Taiwan-adjacent pressure on Pakistan's airspace) just weeks before a planned Trump-Xi meeting. Business and markets outlets are focused on a slumping Chinese AI-stock rally, falling insurer profits, and a weakening EV/NEV sales cycle.

stories.headline: Hong Kong's John Lee apologizes over Tai Po fire, housing chief resigns amid sweeping reforms
stories.summary: Hong Kong's leader publicly apologized for last year's deadly Tai Po blaze that killed 168 people, announcing civil-service and legislative reforms, an overhaul of inspection units, and the resignation of housing chief Winnie Ho. Lee framed the resignation as his own political decision while insisting he would stay in his post.

stories.headline: China's fifth plenum ends with military elevation and deeper party purges
stories.summary: The Chinese Communist Party closed its four-day fifth plenum by elevating a top military official to the Politburo while formalizing expulsions of dozens of senior members, part of Xi Jinping's drive to tighten party discipline. WSJ separately reported Xi is demanding greater loyalty as the purges thin the party elite.

stories.headline: US bans Chinese labs from testing electronics ahead of Trump-Xi summit
stories.summary: Washington banned all Chinese laboratories from certifying electronic devices for the US market just weeks before Trump is due to meet Xi, adding a fresh irritant to the relationship ahead of the summit. Taipei Times separately flagged related US restrictions on Chinese genomics firms.

stories.headline: Pakistan's brief airspace closure to Taiwanese flights fuels 'China squeeze' fears
stories.summary: Taiwan said Pakistan briefly barred its cargo and passenger flights from its airspace citing Beijing's One China policy before reversing course, with Taipei suspecting China was behind the move. Nikkei Asia noted the episode highlights the "precarious operating environment" for Taiwanese firms amid narrowing international space.

stories.headline: China's AI stock rally unwinds as profitability doubts spread
stories.summary: Chinese AI-linked shares have fallen nearly 40% from their June peak, led by state-backed chipmakers, as investors grow wary of the sector's earnings prospects following a parallel US AI stock sell-off. The Economist separately examined why Chinese investors remain unusually glum even as the country pushes an AI-driven growth narrative.

stories.headline: China's NEV retail sales slip as peak-season demand stays weak
stories.summary: New-energy vehicle retail sales fell 13% year-on-year in the first 25 days of October to 753,000 units, roughly flat versus the same period in September, underscoring a soft patch in China's crowded EV market even as automakers like Li Auto and Xpeng rush out refreshed models to compete.

stories.headline: Ping An, CPIC profits plunge as China's stock slide hits insurers
stories.summary: Ping An and China Pacific Insurance reported third-quarter net profit declines of 93.7% and 68.4% respectively as a stock-market downturn hit investment returns, though both avoided the outright losses some analysts had expected across the sector.

stories.headline: Beijing moves to keep labor unrest off the record
stories.summary: A wave of arrests targeting labor activists and reporters, alongside the shutdown of outlets and social accounts covering workplace disputes, suggests Chinese authorities are working to suppress public discussion of labor grievances.

China.gaps: No distinct recent coverage found from Global Times, China Daily, Xinhua, CGTN, Sixth Tone, Yicai Global, or The Wire China beyond their general daily roundups/older Trump-Xi summit pieces; Reuters, AP, and FT provided no feed items for this period.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf, Israeli and pan-Arab outlets is dominated by the inconclusive Israeli election and its regional ripple effects, the intensifying Houthi missile campaign against Saudi Arabia, and volatile oil markets tied to new US-Iran diplomatic contacts. Yemen's worsening humanitarian toll and a wave of Hormuz shipping attacks are also drawing sustained attention.

stories.headline: Netanyahu falls short of majority as opposition, Arab parties win 67 seats
stories.summary: Israel's election produced no clear winner, with Netanyahu's bloc projected at 53 seats and the opposition at 67, leaving Arab-led parties with a record 19 seats as potential kingmakers while Netanyahu's camp alleges foreign interference.

stories.headline: Saudi air defenses shoot down Houthi missiles targeting Riyadh
stories.summary: Saudi forces intercepted two more ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh as part of a weeks-long Houthi bombardment that has already killed civilians and disrupted flights, with Saudi and Yemeni foreign ministers meeting to discuss a response.

stories.headline: Oil prices decline after diplomatic push in Iran war
stories.summary: Brent crude slipped to about $114 a barrel after US Vice President JD Vance reportedly wrote to Iran's security council chief to try to revive peace talks, though Trump downplayed the outreach as being about medical supplies.

stories.headline: Tanker struck by projectile in Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: UKMTO reported a tanker was hit by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, the latest in a string of attacks on commercial vessels in the strategic waterway.

stories.headline: Yemen's hospitals buckle as fighting escalates
stories.summary: Hospitals in Taiz are overwhelmed as renewed fighting floods wards with wounded civilians, including a pregnant woman paralyzed by a bullet, underscoring Yemen's deepening humanitarian crisis.

stories.headline: IMF sets December target to clear Egypt's last programme review
stories.summary: The IMF has set a December deadline to complete the final review of Egypt's loan programme, a key step for continued financial support to Cairo.

stories.headline: UAE sentences eight people to life over arms supplies to Sudan's army
stories.summary: An Emirati court handed down life sentences in a case tied to arms supplies for Sudan's military, amid ongoing tension between Khartoum and Abu Dhabi over the Sudan war and the RSF.

stories.headline: Nearly 90% of energy leaders boosted AI spending last year, Adnoc-Microsoft study finds
stories.summary: A new Adnoc-Microsoft study found that nearly 90% of energy sector leaders increased AI investment over the past year, reflecting the industry's rapid digital push.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No recent Gulf/Middle East coverage found for AGBI, Zawya, or Arabian Business; Reuters, AP, BBC and NYT could not be searched directly and no feed items were provided for them.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage this cycle centers on Africa's biggest-ever stock listing, Russia's charm offensive at its Moscow summit, and intensifying Horn of Africa and Sahel security tensions. Business and economic outlets are also tracking Nigeria's banking and energy sectors, while rights and justice stories from Sudan, Tanzania and DRC round out the agenda.

stories.headline: Dangote Refinery IPO closes nearly 3x oversubscribed
stories.summary: Dangote Refinery and Petrochemicals closed its 44-day IPO with orders almost three times the $1.6bn target, with Aliko Dangote saying subscribers from 120 countries sought a stake in what he called the biggest IPO in African history.

stories.headline: Putin's Russia-Africa summit draws scepticism over economic follow-through
stories.summary: At the third Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow, Putin positioned Russia as an ally against a Western-dominated order, but analysts cited by the outlet questioned whether diplomatic reach can translate into the promised trade, noting Russia-Africa trade of about $27bn in 2025 remains well below its $40bn target.

stories.headline: Ethiopia's new Russian fighter jets escalate Eritrea standoff
stories.summary: Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's acquisition of Russian military hardware is reshaping Ethiopia's air power and raising questions about how the debt-strapped country is financing the purchases amid rising tension with Eritrea; African Business separately reported Abiy confirmed delivery of 12 Su-35 jets and plans to acquire S-400 air defence systems from Moscow.

stories.headline: US sanctions on Rwanda spark mixed reactions in Goma
stories.summary: Residents of Goma voiced cautious hope that new US sanctions tied to the conflict in eastern DRC could help break the deadlock between Kinshasa and Kigali-backed forces.

stories.headline: UAE sentences eight to life over arms supplies to Sudan's army
stories.summary: A UAE court handed life sentences to eight defendants over arms supplies to Sudan's army, a ruling that comes amid simmering tension between Khartoum and Abu Dhabi over the Sudan war and the RSF.

stories.headline: Algeria prepares troop deployment in Niger to protect oil assets
stories.summary: Algiers is planning to send military units to Niger to safeguard Sonatrach's oil exploration projects while deepening security cooperation with Niamey, extending its regional footprint.

stories.headline: Tanzania marks one year since deadly election violence with calls for justice
stories.summary: Tanzanians marked the anniversary of the country's worst election violence, which killed hundreds last year, with renewed demands for accountability.

stories.headline: African banks grew bigger in 2025, but not necessarily stronger
stories.summary: The outlet's Top 300 Finance Champions ranking found many African banks saw balance sheets inflated by currency moves, sovereign debt and recapitalisation rather than underlying improvement, with Nigerian lenders slipping while South African groups advanced.

Africa.gaps: The Continent had no fresh (last 48h) coverage available beyond older archived issues. Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so their current Africa coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past two days centers on the escalating fight between news publishers and Meta over AI content terms, press-freedom crackdowns in Egypt and India, and the fallout from a New York Times investigation into Alaska's Senate race just before the U.S. midterms. Business-of-media stories include layoffs at People Inc., AI-related friction in the music industry, and a wave of dealmaking tied to RedBird Capital's recent acquisition of Puck.

stories.headline: Publishers Escalate Fight Over Meta's New AI Content Terms
stories.summary: Meta pledged to hold a full consultation with news industry leaders before finalizing controversial new content terms, even if it causes further delay, while Norwegian publishers including Schibsted and NRK won a court victory seeking an injunction and a global publisher coalition is demanding Meta stop using their content without permission.

stories.headline: NYT's Dual-Dan-Sullivan Investigation Roils Alaska Senate Race
stories.summary: The New York Times published a report on two candidates named Dan Sullivan running in Alaska's Senate race that has reportedly drawn a furious response from President Trump toward the Democratic candidate, and is now a major talking point among TV and political media.

stories.headline: Egypt Fines Editor Lina Attalah, Shuts Down Mada Masr
stories.summary: An Egyptian court convicted independent news outlet Mada Masr's editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, of running an unlicensed website, and authorities shut the outlet down, raising fresh alarm over press freedom under Cairo's government.

stories.headline: People Inc. Cuts 195 Staffers Amid Media Upheaval
stories.summary: Dotdash Meredith's People Inc. eliminated 195 jobs, citing rapid changes across the media industry, continuing a broader pattern of newsroom and digital-publisher contraction.

stories.headline: India's Crackdown on the Press
stories.summary: Independent New Delhi journalist Fatima Khan told CJR that press freedom in India is diminishing under government pressure, though she expressed hope that a younger generation of journalists can push back.

stories.headline: RedBird and Guy Oseary Launch $1 Billion Tech-Media Fund
stories.summary: RedBird Capital Partners, which recently acquired a majority stake in Puck at a roughly $250 million valuation, teamed with Guy Oseary's Sound Ventures to launch a new $1 billion fund targeting tech, media and culture investments.

stories.headline: Universal Music Group Targets 'AI Slop' as Q3 Revenue Hits $3.78B
stories.summary: UMG CEO Lucian Grainge used the company's Q3 earnings call, where revenue hit $3.78 billion, to push streaming services to pay out less for AI-generated music than for tracks by real artists.

stories.headline: Tommy Robinson Found Guilty of Harassing Daily Mail Journalists
stories.summary: A UK court found Tommy Robinson (Stephen Yaxley-Lennon) guilty of harassing Daily Mail journalists, with sentencing scheduled for December 16.

Media.gaps: No feed items were supplied for NYT, WSJ or FT and these outlets block web search, so no current coverage from them could be verified beyond The Guardian's Egypt press-freedom story. Status and Puck's homepages could not be searched for stories within the last 48 hours; search results for both returned only older archived pages (e.g. Puck's media category page showed items from mid-to-late October but nothing confirmed within the strict 24-48h window), so no dedicated items from them are included.
